column1: 5:1|These are the descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn. He was the firstborn, but when he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. The genealogy was not to be reckoned by birthright.|Distinguish birth order, transferred rights, and genealogical reckoning without forcing the last clause’s subject.
5:2|Judah became strong among his brothers, and a ruler came from him, but the birthright belonged to Joseph.|Keep political leadership distinct from Joseph’s birthright.
5:3|Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, had these sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.|Retain the repeated firstborn designation and all four names.
5:4|Joel’s line continued through his son Shemaiah, then Gog, then Shimei,|Render successive his-son links as a descending line.
5:5|then Micah, Reaiah, Baal,|Continue the same generations across the verse break.
5:6|and Beerah, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria deported. Beerah was a leader of the Reubenites.|Name the deported leader clearly and retain Chronicles’ royal-name form.
5:7|His relatives, listed by clans in their genealogical records, included Jeiel the head, Zechariah,|Keep the clan register distinct from the direct line.
5:8|and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. Bela lived in Aroer, with his territory extending to Nebo and Baal-meon.|Make the named resident clear without losing ancestry or boundaries.

5:9|To the east he occupied land as far as the edge of the wilderness stretching from the Euphrates River, because their herds had grown numerous in Gilead.|Preserve the geographic reach and the reason for expansion.
5:10|In Saul’s days they made war on the Hagrites and defeated them. They settled in their tents throughout the region east of Gilead.|Keep war, displacement, and occupation in sequence.
5:11|The descendants of Gad lived beside them in Bashan, as far as Salecah.|Locate Gad relative to Reuben.
5:12|Joel was the head, Shapham second, with Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.|Retain named ranks without inventing a fuller hierarchy.
5:13|Their relatives by ancestral household were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven.|Preserve seven distinct household names.
5:14|They were descendants of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.|Keep every link in the ascending pedigree.
5:15|Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, headed their ancestral household.|Identify Ahi’s leadership and both ancestors.
5:16|They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and in all Sharon’s pasturelands out to their boundaries.|Retain all three settlement descriptions.
5:17|All of them were entered in genealogical records in the days of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.|Keep both royal reference points without harmonizing chronology.

5:18|The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh had 44,760 capable fighting men, trained for war, who carried shield and sword and drew the bow.|Keep the exact total and distinct military skills.
5:19|They fought the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.|Retain all four opposing groups.

5:20|They received help against them, and the Hagrites and all their allies were handed over to them. They had cried out to God during the battle, and he answered because they trusted him.|Preserve the narrator’s explanation of the victory.

5:21|They captured the livestock: fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep and goats, and two thousand donkeys. They also took a hundred thousand people captive.|Distinguish captive people from the livestock while preserving all counts.
5:22|Many fell slain, because the battle was from God. The victors lived in their place until the exile.|Keep the attribution of battle to God and the resulting deaths.

5:23|The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon. They had become numerous.|Preserve the three northern place names and population growth.

5:24|Their ancestral household heads were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty warriors, men of renown, heads of their ancestral households.|Retain the repeated household designation and all seven leaders.

5:25|But they were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors. They went whoring after the gods of the peoples of the land whom God had destroyed before them.|Keep the religious infidelity image and the destruction of earlier peoples.

5:26|So the God of Israel stirred the spirit of Pul king of Assyria and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria. He deported the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they remain to this day.|Retain both royal designations and the narrator’s divine agency claim.
6:1|Levi’s sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.|Retain the three foundational Levitical lines.
6:2|Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.|Keep all four names in source order.
6:3|Amram’s children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.|Use children for the explicitly mixed sibling group and sons for Aaron’s male descendants.
6:4|Eleazar fathered Phinehas, and Phinehas fathered Abishua.|Keep successive fatherhood links explicit.
6:5|Abishua fathered Bukki, and Bukki fathered Uzzi.|Preserve the two-generation sequence.
6:6|Uzzi fathered Zerahiah, and Zerahiah fathered Meraioth.|Keep each father linked to his named son.
6:7|Meraioth fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.|Retain the repeated fathered pattern through the pedigree.
6:8|Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Ahimaaz.|Keep the priestly line’s two links.
6:9|Ahimaaz fathered Azariah, and Azariah fathered Johanan.|Preserve the sequence before the next Azariah.
6:10|Johanan fathered Azariah, who served as priest in the house Solomon built in Jerusalem.|Keep the second Azariah and his temple service.
6:11|Azariah fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.|Retain repeated names rather than merging generations.
6:12|Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Shallum.|Keep this Zadok’s place in the later line.
6:13|Shallum fathered Hilkiah, and Hilkiah fathered Azariah.|Preserve the Hilkiah-to-Azariah link.
6:14|Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak.|Keep the final two fatherhood links before exile.
6:15|Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD deported Judah and Jerusalem through Nebuchadnezzar.|Preserve the LORD’s agency and the named human agent.
6:16|Levi’s sons were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.|Retain Gershom here alongside Gershon in verse 1.
6:17|Gershom’s sons were named Libni and Shimei.|Keep both sons and the naming formula.
6:18|Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.|Retain the deliberate repetition of the four branches.
6:19|Merari’s sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levitical clans by their ancestry.|Close the clan introduction while keeping both sons.
6:20|Gershom’s line ran through Libni his son, then Jahath, then Zimmah,|Clarify that the list descends through successive generations.
6:21|then Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai.|Continue the descending line across the verse break.
6:22|Kohath’s line ran through Amminadab his son, then Korah, then Assir,|Keep Amminadab as written rather than harmonizing to Izhar.
6:23|then Elkanah, Ebiasaph, and Assir,|Retain the second Assir in this sequence.
6:24|then Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.|Complete the descending sequence without dropping names.
6:25|Elkanah’s sons were Amasai and Ahimoth.|Keep the two sons as a separate branching notice.
6:26|Elkanah: the descendants of Elkanah continued through Zophai his son, then Nahath,|Retain the difficult repeated Elkanah with the read descendants form; explain uncertainty in a note.
6:27|then Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah.|Preserve these forms rather than harmonizing with verses 34–35.
6:28|Samuel’s sons were Vashni the firstborn, and Abijah.|Retain the difficult pinned wording rather than silently supplying Joel.
6:29|Merari’s line ran through Mahli, then Libni his son, Shimei, and Uzzah,|Preserve the descending sequence from Merari through Mahli.
6:30|then Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah.|Complete Merari’s line in the stated order.
6:31|These are the men David put in charge of song in the LORD’s house after the ark came to rest.|Link the musicians’ appointment with the resting ark.

6:32|They served with song before the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the LORD’s house in Jerusalem. They carried out their service according to their assigned order.|Keep the transition from tent to temple and ordered service.

6:33|These are the men who served, together with their sons. From the Kohathites: Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,|Introduce the singer’s ascending pedigree without confusing it with earlier descending lists.
6:34|son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,|Preserve Eliel and Toah as this record gives them.
6:35|son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,|Follow the read Zuph and retain all four links.
6:36|son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,|Preserve the repeated Elkanah and Joel in the longer pedigree.
6:37|son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,|Keep each link leading back to Korah.
6:38|son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.|Complete Heman’s ancestry to Israel.
6:39|His fellow musician Asaph stood at his right. Asaph was the son of Berechiah, son of Shimea,|Render brother as a fellow Levite here, not a claim that Heman and Asaph share a father.
6:40|son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah,|Keep Asaph’s three successive ancestors.
6:41|son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,|Continue the pedigree in source order.
6:42|son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,|Preserve this Ethan as a distinct ancestor in Asaph’s line.
6:43|son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.|Complete Asaph’s Gershomite ancestry.
6:44|Their fellow Levites, the Merarites, stood at the left: Ethan son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,|Make the left-hand group and its singer clear.
6:45|son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,|Keep Ethan’s three ancestry links.
6:46|son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,|Retain the names without importing parallel forms.
6:47|son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.|Preserve the Mahli–Mushi relationship as this pedigree states it.
6:48|Their fellow Levites were assigned all the other work of the tabernacle, the house of God.|Distinguish the broader Levitical service from the singers’ work.

6:49|Aaron and his sons made offerings on the altar of burnt offering and the incense altar. They carried out all the work of the Most Holy Place and made atonement for Israel, just as Moses, God’s servant, had commanded.|Keep Aaron’s distinct duties and the atonement language.
6:50|Aaron’s line ran through Eleazar his son, then Phinehas, then Abishua,|Introduce another descending priestly line clearly.
6:51|then Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah,|Continue the same three links without changing direction.
6:52|then Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub,|Keep all three generations in source order.
6:53|then Zadok and Ahimaaz.|Close the line at Ahimaaz as the source does.

6:54|These were their settlements, with their encampments in their territory. The descendants of Aaron, of the Kohathite clan, received an allotment.|Preserve the territorial introduction and priority of Aaron’s lot.
6:55|They were given Hebron in Judah and the pastureland around it.|Distinguish the town’s pastureland from the fields in the next verse.
6:56|But the town’s fields and villages were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.|Retain the exception for Caleb’s property.

6:57|Aaron’s descendants were given the refuge towns: Hebron; Libnah with its pastureland; Jattir; Eshtemoa with its pastureland;|Retain the difficult plural refuge-towns heading without silently correcting it.
6:58|Hilen with its pastureland; Debir with its pastureland;|Keep both grants and their recurring pastureland formula.
6:59|Ashan with its pastureland; and Beth-shemesh with its pastureland.|Preserve these town names rather than replacing them from Joshua.

6:60|From Benjamin they received Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth, each with its pastureland. Their clans received thirteen towns in all.|Keep the reported total despite fewer surviving names in this list.
6:61|The remaining Kohathite descendants received ten towns by lot from the tribal clans, from the half-tribe of Manasseh.|Retain the compressed and difficult allocation wording, with a note.
6:62|The Gershomite clans received thirteen towns from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh in Bashan.|Keep the four tribal sources and thirteen-town total.
6:63|The Merarite clans received twelve towns by lot from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.|Preserve the three tribal sources and twelve-town count.
6:64|The Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands.|Keep the summary of the land grants.
6:65|They assigned by lot the towns named above from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.|Preserve all three tribes in the retrospective allocation notice.
6:66|Some Kohathite clans received towns in the territory of Ephraim.|Introduce the geographical list for the other Kohathites.
6:67|They were given the refuge towns: Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim with its pastureland, and Gezer with its pastureland;|Keep the plural heading and specific hill-country setting.
6:68|Jokmeam with its pastureland; Beth-horon with its pastureland;|Retain both allotments and their land.
6:69|Aijalon with its pastureland; and Gath-rimmon with its pastureland.|Preserve the paired towns without harmonizing tribal geography.
6:70|From the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner and Bileam, each with its pastureland, were given to the remaining Kohathite clans.|Identify the recipients and preserve these distinctive town forms.
6:71|The Gershomites received Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, each with its pastureland, from the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh.|Keep both Bashan grants and their tribal source.
6:72|From Issachar: Kedesh with its pastureland, Daberath with its pastureland,|Retain the two towns under their tribal heading.
6:73|Ramoth with its pastureland, and Anem with its pastureland.|Keep Ramoth and Anem as the pinned list names them.
6:74|From Asher: Mashal with its pastureland, Abdon with its pastureland,|Preserve the paired Asher grants.
6:75|Hukok with its pastureland, and Rehob with its pastureland.|Retain Hukok instead of harmonizing to a parallel place name.
6:76|From Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kiriathaim, each with its pastureland.|Keep all three towns and the Galilee qualifier.
6:77|The remaining Merarites received Rimmono and Tabor, each with its pastureland, from Zebulun.|Retain the source’s two named Zebulun grants.

6:78|Across the Jordan, east of the river opposite Jericho, they received from Reuben Bezer in the wilderness with its pastureland, and Jahzah with its pastureland;|Make the east-Jordan location clear while retaining both grants.
6:79|Kedemoth with its pastureland; and Mephaath with its pastureland.|Keep the final two Reubenite towns.
6:80|From Gad: Ramoth in Gilead with its pastureland, Mahanaim with its pastureland,|Retain the Gilead location and both grants.
6:81|Heshbon with its pastureland, and Jazer with its pastureland.|Close the town list with both Gadite grants intact.
7:1|Issachar’s sons were Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron—four.|Follow the read Jashub and preserve the four-son total.

7:2|Tola’s sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel. They headed Tola’s ancestral households, mighty warriors listed by their generations. In David’s days they numbered 22,600.|Keep all six heads and the exact census total.
7:3|Uzzi’s son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah’s sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah—five heads in all.|Preserve the five-head count without inventing a fifth son.
7:4|With them, by generation and ancestral household, were 36,000 troops ready for war, for they had many wives and sons.|Retain the stated connection between household size and troop numbers.
7:5|Their relatives throughout Issachar’s clans were mighty warriors, 87,000 in all according to their genealogical records.|Preserve the larger tribal total separately.
7:6|Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.|Keep this three-name list distinct from chapter 8.

7:7|Bela’s sons were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri—five ancestral household heads and mighty warriors. Their genealogical records listed 22,034.|Retain the unusually precise total and all five heads.
7:8|Becher’s sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were Becher’s sons.|Preserve the list’s closing repetition and nine names.
7:9|Their genealogical records, arranged by generations and ancestral household heads, listed 20,200 mighty warriors.|Keep the census organization and exact total.
7:10|Jediael’s son was Bilhan. Bilhan’s sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.|Follow the read Jeush and retain each son.
7:11|All these were Jediael’s descendants, ancestral household heads and mighty warriors, with 17,200 men able to go out to war.|Preserve the number and qualification for service.
7:12|Shuppim and Huppim were descendants of Ir; Hushim was a descendant of Aher.|Retain the compressed family links without silently moving Hushim to Dan.
7:13|Naphtali’s sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, descendants of Bilhah.|Keep the maternal ancestry as well as four male names.
7:14|Manasseh’s descendants included Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bore. She also bore Machir, Gilead’s father.|Make the woman’s role visible while noting the compressed syntax.

7:15|Machir took a wife from Huppim and Shuppim. His sister’s name was Maacah. The second was named Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had daughters.|Retain the difficult connections and the daughters; explain uncertainty in a note.
7:16|Machir’s wife Maacah bore a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, whose sons were Ulam and Rakem.|Keep Maacah’s naming action and the brother’s descendants.
7:17|Ulam’s son was Bedan. These were descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh.|Preserve the summary pedigree back to Manasseh.
7:18|His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.|Retain the sister’s role without forcing the pronoun’s antecedent.
7:19|Shemida’s sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.|Keep all four names in sequence.
7:20|Ephraim’s line continued through Shuthelah, then Bered his son, Tahath, Eleadah, and Tahath,|Keep the repeated Tahath and the descending order.

7:21|then Zabad and Shuthelah. Ezer and Elead were killed by the men native to Gath, because they had gone down to take their livestock.|Retain the raid and deaths without resolving the uncertain direction of the raid.
7:22|Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.|Preserve prolonged grief and the family’s response.
7:23|He slept with his wife, and she conceived and bore a son. He named him Beriah because disaster had come upon his house.|Keep the naming response to household disaster.
7:24|His daughter Sheerah built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah.|Keep the daughter as the builder of all three places.
7:25|His son was Rephah; also Resheph, then Telah his son, and Tahan,|Preserve the uneven genealogy rather than inventing an explicit Rephah–Resheph link.
7:26|then Ladan, Ammihud, Elishama,|Continue the descending line across labels.
7:27|Nun, and Joshua.|Complete the ancestry at Joshua without expanding the verse.

7:28|Their holdings and settlements included Bethel and its villages; Naaran to the east; Gezer and its villages to the west; and Shechem and its villages, as far as Ayyah and its villages.|Keep the directional markers and each group of villages.

7:29|Along Manasseh’s territory were Beth-shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, each with its villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these places.|Preserve the four settlements and Joseph’s encompassing family identity.
7:30|Asher’s sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah; Serah was their sister.|Keep the explicitly named sister distinct from the sons.
7:31|Beriah’s sons were Heber and Malchiel, the father of Birzaith.|Follow the read Birzaith and retain the father designation.
7:32|Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.|Keep Shua in the sibling list.
7:33|Japhlet’s sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were Japhlet’s sons.|Preserve the repeated framing of the three-name list.
7:34|Shemer’s sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.|Follow the read Rohgah and Hubbah while retaining Shemer’s form.
7:35|His brother Helem’s sons were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.|Keep the brother relationship and four sons.
7:36|Zophah’s sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,|Open the eleven-name list without reducing it.
7:37|Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.|Complete Zophah’s list in its stated order.
7:38|Jether’s sons were Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.|Retain Jether rather than harmonizing to Ithran.
7:39|Ulla’s sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.|Keep the separate three-son household.

7:40|All these were Asher’s descendants: ancestral household heads, chosen men, mighty warriors, and leading chiefs. Their genealogical records listed 26,000 men available for military service.|Retain the leadership descriptions and military total.
8:1|Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,|Keep birth order explicit in this five-son list.
8:2|Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.|Complete the ordered list without harmonizing chapter 7.
8:3|Bela’s sons were Addar, Gera, Abihud,|Start Bela’s list with its first three names.
8:4|Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,|Continue the same list across labels.
8:5|Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.|Retain the repeated Gera rather than deleting a name.
8:6|These were Ehud’s descendants, ancestral heads of the people living in Geba, who were deported to Manahath:|Keep the displacement while leaving its broader historical setting unstated.
8:7|Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera. Gera deported them; he fathered Uzza and Ahihud.|Preserve Gera’s agency and the subsequent fatherhood notice.
8:8|Shaharaim had children in the country of Moab after sending away his wives Hushim and Baara.|Retain the dismissal of the wives and the Moab setting.
8:9|By his wife Hodesh he fathered Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,|Name the mother and begin her children’s list.
8:10|Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah. These sons of his were ancestral household heads.|Complete the seven sons and their household role.
8:11|By Hushim he fathered Abitub and Elpaal.|Keep the return to the earlier wife’s children.
8:12|Elpaal’s sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod with its villages.|Retain Shemed as the builder and both towns.
8:13|Beriah and Shema headed the ancestral households of Aijalon’s residents. They drove out the people of Gath.|Keep the leaders’ military action explicit.
8:14|Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,|Begin the list whose parent is named in verse 16.
8:15|Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,|Continue the six earlier names toward the closing family label.
8:16|Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were Beriah’s sons.|Complete the list and make its parent clear at the source’s closing point.
8:17|Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,|Begin Elpaal’s next listed household.
8:18|Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were Elpaal’s sons.|Close the list with the father’s identity.
8:19|Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,|Begin Shimei’s sons in source order.
8:20|Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,|Preserve the middle of Shimei’s list.
8:21|Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were Shimei’s sons.|Close the list without changing Shimei to Shema.
8:22|Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,|Begin Shashak’s sons with all three names.
8:23|Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,|Keep these repeated names within their own household.
8:24|Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,|Continue Shashak’s list across labels.
8:25|Iphdeiah, and Penuel were Shashak’s sons.|Follow the read Penuel and close the household list.
8:26|Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,|Retain Athaliah as a male family member in this list.
8:27|Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were Jeroham’s sons.|Complete the six-name list with its father.
8:28|These were ancestral household heads, leaders listed by their generations. They lived in Jerusalem.|Retain the summary’s repeated leadership emphasis.
8:29|The father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon. His wife was named Maacah.|Do not supply Jeiel from chapter 9 where this verse leaves him unnamed.
8:30|His firstborn son was Abdon; then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,|Keep the firstborn distinction and subsequent names.
8:31|Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher.|Retain Zecher rather than harmonizing to Zechariah in chapter 9.
8:32|Mikloth fathered Shimeah. They too lived in Jerusalem with their relatives, opposite their relatives’ homes.|Keep the relationship and residential proximity.
8:33|Ner fathered Kish, and Kish fathered Saul. Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.|Preserve all four sons and the Esh-baal name.
8:34|Jonathan’s son was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.|Keep Merib-baal rather than replacing the name with Mephibosheth.
8:35|Micah’s sons were Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.|Preserve all four sons as this list gives them.
8:36|Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri, and Zimri fathered Moza.|Retain Jehoaddah here beside Jarah in chapter 9.
8:37|Moza fathered Binea. His line continued through Raphah, then Eleasah, then Azel.|Make the descending sequence clear while preserving Raphah’s form.
8:38|Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were Azel’s sons.|Keep Bocheru as a name and the stated six total.
8:39|His brother Eshek’s sons were Ulam the firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.|Preserve the brother relationship and all birth ranks.

8:40|Ulam’s sons were mighty warriors skilled with the bow. They had many sons and grandsons—one hundred fifty. All these belonged to Benjamin.|Retain military skill, the descendant total, and the tribal conclusion.

9:1|All Israel was enrolled in genealogies, recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Judah was deported to Babylon for its unfaithfulness.|Keep the transition from genealogies to the exile’s stated cause.
9:2|The first to settle in their holdings in their towns were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.|Retain all four groups without making temple servants priests.
9:3|People from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh settled in Jerusalem.|Preserve the presence of both northern and southern tribes.
9:4|Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, belonged to the descendants of Perez son of Judah.|Follow the read Bani plus from rather than treating the written form as Benjamin.
9:5|From the Shilonites came Asaiah the firstborn and his sons.|Retain Shilonites as written with the possible Shelah connection noted.
9:6|From Zerah’s descendants came Jeuel. Their relatives numbered six hundred ninety.|Keep the family entry and its stated total.
9:7|From Benjamin came Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah;|Preserve Sallu’s full ancestry.
9:8|Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.|Keep the three separate pedigrees distinct.
